name: agent-fs-planned-units
body:
Planned-unit handoff for `solution.component.agent-fs-tool-suite`. The three new tool files do not exist in the branch graph, so they cannot yet be `implemented-by` targets. The plan-writer declares them as planned Implementation nodes at their real code FQNs (File kind), each the target of a `creates` task:

  opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts
  opencode-suite/tools/apg_mv.ts
  opencode-suite/tools/apg_cp.ts

Once they exist, `solution.component.agent-fs-tool-suite` —implemented-by→ each of them. The component's current resolving anchor is `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (the shared plumbing the tools reuse/extend). The install registry (`solution.component.agent-fs-install-registry`) is anchored on the module `rust.apg.install` because `SUITE_TOOLS` is a `const`, which the code graph does not model as its own node.

Test-tier split (per `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries`): the fs tools' executable path logic is real I/O (filesystem), hence e2e — exercised against a scratch `/tmp` repo per `global.constraint.no-real-project-test`; any pure helper added to `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (path normalization / containment / granted-glob-match decision) belongs in the `bun test` unit tier (`opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`), side-effect-free. The self-enforcement path — resolve the target against the caller's project directory, read the acting agent's granted globs, and decide in/out of scope — is the I/O-bound e2e path; the pure glob-match decision is the unit-tier helper.
